The effect of a genetic mutation has to be extreme enough to make a real impact on an individuals fitness. Evolution has a much stronger reaction to -lets say- muscular distrophy than it has to an individual who is cross eyed due to inbreeding. Similarly Evolution will a smaller impact to said inbred cross eyed person, than to an inbred individual who has autism.

Although inbreeding has created this cross eyed person, it does not stop them from reproducing. Said individual can find a mate who is genetically dissimilar, whereby reducing the inbreeding effect on offspring. At the end of the inbred person's life he/she can end up with just as many normal phenotype children as a non-inbred person. Although our cross eyed example is likley to pass on some minor health issues, evolution will not strongly select against his/her lineage. Whereas cross eye's autistic sister/cousin is unlikely to find a mate or produce children. It's really important to understand that evolution has strong and weak selective pressure. Not all disadvantages will be bred out of our population because most of them don't have a significant impact on our evolutionary fitness.
